producer_report.summary: `carry` in reading.rs now appends, for each failed check in the job's final verification, an entry with the check name, command, exit code and output tail. It goes after the findings and reasons. The output is cut to its last 1024 bytes using the existing `checks::tail`, then redacted by the same `redact_all` call as the other carried text. Passing checks add nothing. Retried jobs and jobs named by id both use `carry`, so both get it. The two brief headings in briefs.rs now say the findings include failed-check output, and the retry one labels it as quoted data. I added CHANGELOG entry. New tests cover a failed check with output, a passing check's output being left out, the size cap, redaction, and a verification with no failed checks. The lifecycle test checks the 'try again on <job>' brief. `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` all pass.

checks_run.note: Includes the new unit tests carry_adds_only_failed_checks_after_the_reasons_redacted_and_bounded and carry_without_failed_checks_adds_nothing, and the new lifecycle test try_again_on_a_job_rejected_by_a_check_carries_the_failed_checks_output.

open_issues: The redaction and size-cap criteria are tested in a unit test on carry(), not in the lifecycle test. The lifecycle test checks that the failed check's output is carried and the passing one's is not. It cannot show carry-time redaction, because the recorded output was already redacted when the check ran.
The 1024-byte cap is my choice; the brief said only 'modest'.
mistakes: One Edit call used a wrong file path and failed harmlessly. It changed nothing.
learnings: Check output_tail is already redacted and tailed to 4096 bytes when the check runs (checks.rs), so the carry-time redaction is a second pass.
The lifecycle fixture's checks print nothing; the lifecycle test builds a custom config with Fixture::with_config to give the checks distinctive output.
A secret-shaped test string has to be built at run time (e.g. concat), since the repo's secret scan rejects literal tokens.
